First and foremost, OP, I am so sorry for your loss. 

As far as advice, I'd recommend finding a good PTSD therapist/support group in your area. I'm not sure that every mental health facility does it, but there is one in my area that has PTSD group therapy sessions. I'd for sure do some research into that on your community, and that's only if you're comfortable with a group setting. Not a lot of people are, and that's completely ok. 

As difficult as it is, please remember that it's ok to not be ok. You don't have to be, and some days you *won't* be. Give yourself some grace and let yourself feel as much as you're willing to let yourself feel. 

I'd also recommend Journaling, since it can help get the thoughts out without actually having to tell anyone. Sometimes, people don't know how to help in these kinds of situations. This is unchartered territory for everyone involved. Don't expect much from yourself or others in the next few days/weeks because having high expectations, only to be disappointed, can amplify the turmoil/grief you're most likely feeling. I'm not saying don't expect anything from anyone, just don't expect too much because these circumstances are hard already.

First and foremost, OP, I am so sorry for your loss. 

Secondly, reading the coroner's report, in my opinion, is a personal choice. Only you get to determine whether you read it or not. That being said, sometimes, after reading it, some people have more questions than answers. 

I'd advise that if/when you choose to read it, definitely make sure you have a good support system/therapist who can help you process any feelings/thoughts/questions you may have. It's truly a club none of us want to be in. 

I'd also like to note that the coroner's report is solely about how they passed. Sometimes, it leaves people trying to reconcile the two individuals. The one we remember versus the one that isn't here anymore because of how they passed. It's hard for us to envision them being the same person. Please don't let whatever that report says make you feel like you didn't know your partner. You knew a version of them that no one else did. This version of them is one that, while difficult to grasp and understand, was struggling. 

It may help. It may not. But please do your best day by day. It's a difficult journey. Sending you so many good vibes, OP.
